spec.question: E207 measured that a count can sit under a gap/level name. E208 asks the class table itself: with the count vocabulary added, which cells does the level-quote audit stop quoting, and what does each one cost?
spec.why_pruned: on the live tree every cell these words matched was a real non-integral bp reading, so the guard refuses to retire them; the hits are published under rejected_word_hits instead
spec.matching: whole token only, so `members` is a count and `membership_bp` is not; the guard runs before the offset/derived shape rules, because `gap_sessions` would otherwise be read as an offset first

readers.current: level_class() -- count guard, then the same table

spec.changes_nothing_else: no value is re-derived and no producer is touched; the only change is which cells the name channel files as a level

honest: a count word is a declaration about the NAME, not proof about the value: an integer under `days` could in principle be a coarse bp reading, which is why every moved cell is published with its face, path and value instead of being dropped silently
this leg can shrink the level-quote audit's totals; that shrinkage is the finding, not a regression -- the retired cells were never bp quotes
the vocabulary is closed and hand-written, so a count spelled without one of these words is still read as a level: the list is the whole coverage claim
law_ref: E207-COUNT-AS-QUOTE-AUDIT (pool entry of the same round) + O-20261002-2100
